New model

Gemini 4 Neon arrives

18 November 2026 · Reading time: 4 minutes · Audio in the app: 5 minutes. Listening to the briefing is part of Sapaude Premium.

Google has released Gemini 4 Neon, a model that sits between the fast Hydrogen and the heavy Carbon. Google pitches it for coding, office work and science, at a lower cost per task than Carbon.

Sapaude retells the story in its own words. The source is below. Publisher: Sapaude.

In three points

Three points, in this order: what the source shows, where that claim stops, and what to check next.

  1. Google says Neon ranks third overall with a score of 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its highest thinking level, just behind larger, slower models.
  2. It costs $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens and has a 1 million-token context window. At the default setting, Google puts the cost per task 32 percent below Carbon.
  3. Neon is rolling out in the paid Gemini API, Gemini for business, Antigravity and the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra subscribers.

A model for the middle

Google introduced Gemini 4 Neon on November 18, 2026. Koray Kavukcuoglu, SVP at Google DeepMind and Google's Chief AI Architect, describes it as "frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion" across software engineering, knowledge work and science. In the Gemini 4 family it sits between Hydrogen, the small and fast workhorse, and Carbon, which Google recommends for its hardest extended projects.

The model costs $3 per million input tokens, $0.15 for cached input, and $15 per million output tokens. The context window holds 1 million tokens, enough for Google to pitch spreadsheets, PDFs, charts, audio and video in one request that comes back as a structured deliverable.

What Google claims

At its highest thinking level, xhigh, Neon ranks third overall on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 61, according to Google. It is second on the Vals Index and second for steerability on Agent Arena, which measures how cleanly a model adapts to corrections in the middle of a task. Google also reports its lowest fabrication rate yet in internal Antigravity testing.

There are four thinking levels. At the default, high, Google says Neon's cost per task is 32 percent lower than Carbon's.

Built for long coding sessions

In Antigravity, Google's agent coding environment, Neon can work alone or as an orchestrator that directs parallel Hydrogen agents. Google says it rereads fewer files, shares progress as it works and compacts context reliably in long sessions. The harness matters: on SWE-sweep, Neon scores 12.8 percent with the mini-SWE setup and 39.0 percent inside Antigravity.

Google's demos include a WebGL2 ski simulator on real Mont Blanc terrain and a 100,000-cell Google Sheet that relights a photo with more than 500,000 formulas.

Who gets it

Neon is rolling out in the paid tier of the Gemini API in Google AI Studio, in Gemini for business, in Antigravity for paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers, and in the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra. VentureBeat notes that the launch post gives no absolute completion times for matched Neon and Carbon jobs. All benchmark figures are Google's own selection.

What you can do

Neon is Google's bid to move frequent hard work off its most expensive model. The rankings and cost figures come from Google's launch post, and the lowest fabrication rate yet is an internal Antigravity test.

In the app, the same story is also told shorter and in more detail, matched to your level.
